readout_other: Motor-evoked potentials via single-pulse TMS-EMG of the right first dorsal interosseous muscle; Go/No-Go visual reaction-time and accuracy task
direction_notes: 250 kHz unifocal and 825 kHz multi-focal TUS significantly reduced normalized MEP amplitude versus sham (both p=0.018), most evident at 5 and 30 min post-TUS; 825 kHz unifocal showed only a nonsignificant trend toward inhibition (p=0.071). Reaction time and accuracy were unchanged across all conditions.
safety_notes: Participants reported mild-to-moderate symptoms across sessions (most often weakness in hand grip, headache, sleepiness; also neck pain, tingling, itchiness, difficulty paying attention), rated possibly/probably related to stimulation; none were rated severe or definitely related.

target.label: left primary motor cortex (M1), hand-knob/precentral gyrus hotspot

timing.protocol_description: TUS delivered to left M1 at PRF 100 Hz, duty cycle 10%, for 120 s; a total ramp of 25% of the burst duration (12.5% up, 12.5% down) was applied to minimise onset artifacts. MEPs (30 TMS pulses at 120% RMT) and RT/accuracy were assessed at baseline and 5, 30, 60 min post-TUS.

target.label: left primary motor cortex (M1), hand-knob/precentral gyrus hotspot

timing.protocol_description: 825 kHz unifocal TUS delivered for 120 s at PRF 100 Hz, duty cycle 10%. The 825 kHz multi-focal condition electronically cycled three simultaneous foci sequentially (2 s intervals) so each focus received 120 s of effective stimulation, extending total session duration to 360 s; same PRF/duty-cycle/ramping as the unifocal conditions.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Twenty healthy adult volunteers (11 male, 9 female) with no history of neurological or psychiatric conditions were recruited for this study.
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Following this, participants completed four randomized, double-blind experimental sessions: 250 kHz unifocal (250-UF), 825 kHz unifocal (825-UF), 825 kHz multi-focal (825-MF), and sham (figure 2(A)).

flags.reason: Sham was implemented by electronically defocusing the ultrasound (randomized phase settings) rather than an inactive/powered-off transducer, active control site, or sound-only sham; does not cleanly match a listed sham_type category, coded as 'other'.

825 kHz unifocal (120 s) and multi-focal (360 s total, 120 s effective per focus) sessions are combined into one exposure per the target x frequency rule, though they differ in focal pattern (single vs three cycled foci) in addition to duration.
List combines the separately reported Table 1 mean adjusted in situ ISPPA for the 825 kHz unifocal (4.02 W/cm2) and multi-focal (3.38 W/cm2) sessions.

0.5 W/cm2 is the initially intended common in situ ISPTA target stated for all sessions before per-participant safety adjustment; Table 1 only reports adjusted ISPPA (not ISPTA) per session, so the intended value is used here.
